home.faq.title: Things you might ask
home.faq.q1: Is this a template or a framework? Do I own the code after cloning
home.faq.a1: It is a template, not a framework. After cloning you own the full source, modules collaborate through explicit interfaces, you can change or delete any part, no framework conventions to follow and no vendor lock-in
home.faq.q2: Can I delete modules I don't use
home.faq.a2: Yes. Modules collaborate through interfaces, removing payment or AI does not affect auth or storage, you just skip writing the base flow instead of redesigning sign-up, payment and storage from zero
home.faq.q3: I'm not building an AI product, is it still a fit
home.faq.a3: Yes. AI is an optional module, remove it and auth, payment, credits, storage, queues and the deploy skeleton stay complete
home.faq.q4: How much can I actually save? Is the free tier enough to start
home.faq.a4: The free tier is enough to run an MVP, Workers Paid Plan is pay-as-you-go from $5/mo. In a public case a Vercel bill of $800+/mo dropped to under $20 on Cloudflare at the same traffic, and R2 egress is free
home.faq.q5: Once I've used the template, how do I sync later upstream updates
home.faq.a5: The repo keeps an upstream remote, follow SYNC_TEMPLATE.md to selectively merge upstream updates, it is not a one-time copy that cuts you off from the template
home.faq.q6: My project is small, is D1 sharding over-engineering
home.faq.a6: No impact. A small project runs on a single active shard by default, add shards when you scale, new users auto-assigned and existing users never migrate, sharding is a fallback for later, not a burden
home.faq.q7: What do I need to get started? Is init complicated
home.faq.a7: Just Node and pnpm. Give the Quick Start link to an Agent once to install create-opcstack-app, then use the Skill directly for future projects

designSystem.title: Design System
designSystem.description: Every component, every token, every pattern — live and interactive
designSystem.s1.title: Tokens, type, surface
designSystem.s1.desc: The rule is monochrome and quiet. Every interactive element resolves to one ink color; every surface is either pure white, parchment off-white, or near-black
designSystem.s1.b.surfaces.desc: Daytime canvases. Tile alternation is the divider
designSystem.s1.b.ink.desc: A single primary carries every signal
designSystem.s2.title: One ink. Two grammars
designSystem.s2.desc: The pill carries every primary action. The square utility carries every chrome action. Active state is always scale(0.95)
designSystem.s3.title: Inputs that disappear into the page
designSystem.s3.desc: A single height, a single radius, a single border tone. Validation state lives on the surface, never on a shadow
designSystem.s4.title: Surface, signal, structure
designSystem.s4.desc: Cards carry content. Badges carry state. Tables carry data. Nothing competes with the product
designSystem.s4.b.card.desc: Header, title, description, action, content, footer
designSystem.s4.b.item.desc: Media, header, title, description, actions, separator, group
designSystem.s5.title: Wayfinding without noise
designSystem.s5.desc: Tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination, menus — all monochrome, all quiet
designSystem.s6.title: Layers that float, not intrude
designSystem.s6.desc: Dialogs, sheets, drawers, popovers, tooltips — all animate in, all respect the monochrome rule
designSystem.s7.title: Reveal on demand
designSystem.s7.desc: Accordion, collapsible, resizable panes, carousel, calendar — all controlled, all accessible
designSystem.s8.title: Business-layer building blocks
designSystem.s8.desc: Auth cards, header, menus, date filter — the components that ship with OPC Stack out of the box
